S01.why: The second image has slightly crisper bottle details and a convincing reflection on the marble, giving it a more polished homepage-banner finish. Both provide a wide, text-free composition with soft studio lighting, but the second integrates the bottle with the surface more naturally.

S02.why: The first image better matches the requested soft studio lighting and premium minimal look, with an understated background and a believable matte black bottle on pale concrete. Both are square and text-free, but the second’s dramatic spotlight and dark background make it less faithful to the brief.

S03.why: Both reproduce all three required phrases correctly, but the second has a more cohesive warm retro design and an inset poster much closer to the requested 3:4 proportions. Its surrounding blank space would need cropping for printing, whereas the first poster’s unusually tall layout would require more substantial reformatting.

S04.why: The first image delivers the exact requested wording in a bold, readable red-and-white square with a clean, intentional layout. The second also has the correct text, but its stray marks and cropped white shape in the upper-right corner make it look unfinished and less usable.

S05.why: The first result delivers the requested golden, late-afternoon warmth, while the second remains comparatively neutral in the skin, sweater, and background. Although the first is somewhat heavily yellow-tinted, it fulfills the central tonal change more convincingly.

S06.why: The second result removes the people while retaining a more believable, detailed background, including the building, fence, and paths. The first appears to replace much more of the surroundings with a simplified landscape, making it less faithful to keeping everything else unchanged.

S08.why: The two results appear visually identical, with the same face, braids, clothing, pose, and background preserved. Neither has a discernible advantage in face blending, believability, or fidelity to the requested scene.

S09.why: The second keeps the portrait framing stable and shows restrained head turns and a gentle smile, better matching the requested subtle animation. The first introduces a substantial close-up and more noticeable facial-proportion changes, making it less faithful to the original portrait.

S10.why: The first shows the silver-blue car driving on the bridge in warm morning light, with believable wheel blur and widescreen framing. The second keeps the car parked on a display platform with the bridge behind it, missing the requested driving action and location.

S11.why: The second better preserves the poster’s portrait proportions and places it believably beside a road with the bridge behind it, while the first stretches the artwork into a wide format. Both provide a landscape composition, but neither fully meets the exact-design and readability requirement because the poster’s smaller text is visibly garbled.

V01.why: The second result has more convincing foam, wet-sand detail, and subtle framing changes consistent with a gentle camera drift, while retaining the empty sunset beach and text-free vertical composition. Both look suitable for meditation, but the supplied frames cannot verify the 10-second duration or the required waves-only audio.

V02.why: The first gives a cleaner, larger product view with a believable turn and changing glass highlights, while the second adds an unrequested picture-frame border and excessive padding. Although the second meets the square-format requirement better, the first is more faithful to a straightforward perfume animation and more usable as product footage.
